title: Xanthe and the Kitchen
premise: Xanthe, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in quiet ruin, has trained their heart into a well-run venue: beautiful, booked, and closed to guests. When Rafael Amberdale — the estranged heir to the Amberdale estate — begs them to pose as his partner at his family's reunion, Xanthe agrees for one weekend and one fee. But the reunion collides with the estate's dying harvest festival, Rafael's family demands more than performance, and by dessert the fake affection has stopped being an act either of them can safely end. As duty, inheritance, and old wounds close in, Xanthe must choose between lending pieces of themselves and risking the whole heart before the festival's final night — choosing love against every survival instinct they've honed.
about_author: Ansel Nystrom is a former caterer who spent a decade watching love arrive on plates at other people's celebrations. They write romances about people who are very good at hosting happiness and very bad at keeping it.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Opening at a flawless wedding they planned, numb behind the scenes, we learn their creed: the heart is trainable, containable. A call comes from Rafael Amberdale, a stranger with a desperate offer. Beat: competence as armor, loneliness underneath.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He explains the reunion: his grandmother's ultimatum, the family that measures worth in attendance. He offers Xanthe money; Xanthe counters with rules — no touching beyond necessity, no real names in bed, out by Sunday. Beat: two guarded people negotiating intimacy's borders.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The Amberdale estate is crumbling grandeur mid-harvest festival preparations. First tests: shared bedroom, grandmother Odile's piercing scrutiny, a cousin who knew Rafael's ex. Xanthe performs flawlessly and hates how easy it feels. Beat: the mask fitting too well.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the reunion dinner, cornered by family cruelty, Rafael takes Xanthe's hand without thinking — and means it. Later, alone in the orchard, they almost kiss and retreat to the rules. Beat: the first involuntary truth, and the fear it brings.

chapters.title: Festival of Small Repairs
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The festival needs saving and the fake couple becomes its organizers, working side by side — stringing lights, arguing over cider recipes, laughing. Odile watches, softening and scheming. Beat: belonging sneaking in through labor and laughter.

chapters.title: What the Estate Owes
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe discovers Rafael plans to sell the estate after the festival — the reunion was his goodbye tour. Feeling used as set dressing, they confront him; he admits he never intended to stay anywhere. Beat: betrayal reframing every warm moment.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. With Xanthe withdrawn into professionalism, Rafael faces his family alone and fails spectacularly — until he realizes the performance he misses is the true one. He finds Xanthe's old engagement ring photo online and understands their armor. Beat: regret sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Festival eve descends into chaos when the hired band cancels and a storm threatens. Rafael shows up unasked, works through the night beside them, and finally says the real thing: he doesn't want to leave if leaving means leaving them. Beat: confession offered, not yet answered.

chapters.title: Final Night
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. Under festival lights, Rafael publicly refuses the inheritance sale, choosing roots over escape; Odile gives her blessing not to the act but to the truth. Xanthe, terrified, chooses risk over containment and kisses him in front of everyone. Beat: climax — love claimed against duty and fear.

chapters.title: Open Kitchen
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, epilogue tone. Weeks later: the estate hosts its first wedding under new management, Xanthe planning it not as armor but as gift. Rafael learns to stay; Xanthe learns hearts aren't muscles to train but rooms to leave unlocked. Beat: resolution — belonging earned, whole heart given.
